drivingQuestion: Why does the doubt exempt all hundred slaughterers, when the priest could claim from either side — either the animal is the firstborn and wholly his, or it is not and he is owed the gifts?
outcomeNote: Rav Oshaya's restriction of the mishna's case removes the ground of the two-sided claim, and the difficulty is not renewed.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ וְאַמַּאי? יָבֹא עָלָיו כֹּהֵן מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין, וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: אִי בְּכוֹר הוּא – כּוּלֵּיהּ דִּידִי הוּא, וְאִי לָאו בְּכוֹר הוּא – הַב לִי מַתְּנָתַאי.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The mishna teaches that if a firstborn animal was intermingled with one hundred non-sacred animals, each belonging to a different person, all of the animals are excluded from the obligation to give the gifts, due to the uncertainty of which animal is the firstborn. The Gemara asks: «But why» is this the halakha? «Let the priest come upon» each slaughterer with a claim «from two sides,» i.e., «let» the priest «say to him: If» this animal «is a firstborn, it is completely mine; and if it is not a firstborn» but is instead a non-sacred animal, then «give me my gifts.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: בְּבָא לִידֵי כֹּהֵן וּמְכָרוֹ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמוּמוֹ.
segments.en: «Rav Oshaya says» in response: In general, a priest may issue such a claim. But the mishna is dealing with a case «where» the firstborn «came into the possession of» the «priest» when it was unblemished and thereafter it developed a permanent blemish, «and» the priest «sold it to an Israelite in its blemished» state. In such a case, the priest may not demand that the owner give him the entire animal with the claim that it is a firstborn, as he already received it once as a firstborn.

moves.summary: argues that the priest could press each slaughterer with a claim that wins either way, so the mishna's exemption should not stand
moves.about: the priest could press each slaughterer with a claim good from either side — if the animal is the firstborn it is wholly his, and if it is not he is owed the gifts — so the doubt should not exempt anyone
